questions.topic: The Invention of Writing: Before and After
questions.stem:
Read the two statements given below and answer the question that follows.
Statement: Before writing was invented, tools, implements, and other material objects made by humans (artefacts) were the major sources for reconstructing people’s ways of living.
Reason: Once writing existed, written documents alone became the major source, and artefacts were no longer used to reconstruct ways of living.
Which of the following options is correct? (A) Both the statement and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the statement. (B) Both the statement and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the statement. (C) The statement is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the statement and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The statement is true but the reason is false.

questions.stem: A researcher sets out to reconstruct the lives of people who lived in the period from about 3 million years ago to 5000 years ago; explain why it is generally difficult for her to understand their thoughts and ideas, and name the major sources she must work with.

questions.stem: Compare the way events and cultures were dated before writing was invented with the way they are dated for the last 5000 years, and give the reason for the change.

Step 3: Literature (written documents) provides information about names; events; and social, political, and cultural life. Step 4: Written documents mention specific dates of events such as coronation and wars. Step 5: Dating of cultures and events therefore becomes relatively accurate.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: Show, step by step, how early humans in the Indian subcontinent progressed from the large cutting tools of the Palaeolithic to smaller stone tools that made hunting more efficient.

markingPoints.description: The oldest human settlement in the Indian subcontinent dates back to about 2 million years ago (1)
Attirampakkam in Tamil Nadu is dated to about 1.5–1.7 million years ago, and Isampur in Karnataka to 1.2 million years ago (1)
Animal fossils and large cutting tools were found, including handaxes and cleavers, and other tools such as stone scrapers and choppers made of quartzite and limestone (1)
These tools were used to chop animal meat, dig out tubers, scrape animal skin, and cleave animal bones to extract protein-rich marrow (1)
Further progress in hunting and gathering was reflected in smaller stone tools — scrapers, borers, and points — which developed projectiles tipped with sharp points (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Step 1: The oldest human settlement in the Indian subcontinent dates back to about 2 million years ago. Step 2: Attirampakkam in Tamil Nadu is dated to about 1.5–1.7 million years ago; Isampur in Karnataka to 1.2 million years ago. Step 3: Animal fossils and large cutting tools were found there — handaxes and cleavers, plus stone scrapers and choppers made of quartzite and limestone. Step 4: These were used to chop animal meat, dig out tubers, scrape animal skin, and cleave animal bones to extract protein-rich marrow. Step 5: Further progress in hunting and gathering was reflected in smaller stone tools — scrapers, borers, and points — which developed projectiles tipped with sharp points.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: The Invention of Writing: Before and After
questions.stem:
A school museum has opened a new corner on life before writing was invented. In the display case lie stone tools, implements and other material objects made by people long ago, and there is no written record of any kind beside them. A student who visits the corner asks the guide two things: how can anyone know how these people lived if nobody wrote anything down, and how old are the objects? The guide replies that the objects themselves must carry the answer, and that measuring time has always been a problem. The student is not satisfied and wants to know what would change if written documents had existed.

(a) Name the major sources a historian must use to reconstruct the ways of living of people from this period. (b) Explain why the thoughts and ideas of these people are generally difficult to understand. (c) Writing came later. Explain how the arrival of written documents changed the study of people and the dating of events.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) Tools, implements, and other material objects made by humans (artefacts). (b) Artefacts reconstruct people’s ways of living, so the thoughts and ideas of people remain difficult to understand. (c) Both material remains and written documents then became sources, literature giving names, events, and social, political and cultural life, and dating became relatively accurate.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: The Invention of Writing: Before and After
questions.stem:
A history club is planning an exhibition with two equal halves. The left half is labelled ‘before writing’ and covers the long stretch from about 3 million years ago to 5000 years ago. The right half is labelled ‘after writing’ and covers only the last 5000 years, including the present. A member points out that the left half is far longer than the right, and the two members of the club disagree about how much of human history each half actually covers. They also argue about the best sources for each half. The teacher asks them to settle both arguments with figures and with named sources.

(a) State the share of human history that falls under each of the two periods. (b) Name the major sources for reconstructing the ways of living of people in the first period. (c) Compare the sources of the second period with those of the first, and explain what a historian can now know that was out of reach before.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) First: more than 99 per cent. Second: less than 1 per cent. (b) Tools, implements, and other material objects made by humans (artefacts). (c) In the second period both material remains and written documents are sources, and literature gives names, events, and social, political and cultural life, so thoughts and ideas come within reach.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: The Invention of Writing: Before and After
questions.stem:
A local historian is writing the timeline of a kingdom. She has an old written record that mentions the coronation of a ruler and a war, and it gives a date for each. Her colleague, working on an earlier age, has only stone tools and other objects made by people, and no written record at all, so he can only guess at the order of events. The historian wonders whether her dates are as trustworthy as her colleague’s guesses, and she asks a teacher to explain why the two situations are so different. The teacher points out that one kind of evidence carries exact dates and the other does not.

(a) State how precisely events and cultures could be dated before writing was invented. (b) Explain why a written record that mentions the coronation of a ruler and a war makes dating more accurate. (c) Setting dating aside, state one further gain that writing brought to the study of people, and explain it.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) Only approximate, because measurement of time was approximate. (b) Because written documents mention specific dates of events such as coronation and wars, so dating becomes relatively accurate. (c) Literature provides information about names; events; and social, political, and cultural life, so the thoughts and ideas of people can now be understood.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
On an outline map of the world, locate and label the following:
(a) Mesopotamia, the “land in between” drained by the Euphrates and Tigris rivers in West Asia.
(b) The Euphrates River.
(c) The Nile River, along which the Egyptian civilisation grew.
(d) The Huang He, in the basin in northern China where the Chinese civilisation grew.
(e) The Zagros mountains, whose crescent-shaped foothills are known as the fertile crescent.

markingPoints.description: Mesopotamia — the “land in between” in West Asia, drained by the Euphrates and Tigris rivers (1)
Euphrates River — in West Asia, draining Mesopotamia together with the Tigris (1)
Nile River — Egypt, along which the Egyptian civilisation grew (1)
Huang He — northern China, in the basin where the Chinese civilisation grew (1)
Zagros mountains — their crescent-shaped foothills are known as the fertile crescent (1)

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
(a) Mesopotamia — the “land in between” in West Asia, drained by the Euphrates and Tigris rivers; in modern times this region includes mainly Iraq and Kuwait, with some parts of Turkey and southwestern Iran.
(b) Euphrates River — West Asia.
(c) Nile River — Egypt.
(d) Huang He — northern China.
(e) Zagros mountains — their crescent-shaped foothills, stretching from the Mediterranean in the west to the Persian Gulf in the east, are known as the ‘fertile crescent’.
